answer: One defence against Sybil attacks is multi-island thread weaving with vault-sealed checkpoints. A new identity begins with no standing and must weave one thread of verified work across several independent islands: each island's verifier sets a task and seals the finished step in a vault time-lock, so the next step opens only after a delay. Since checkpoints must arrive in order, an attacker cannot run many identities in parallel or copy one thread onto another. Faking a hundred agents thus means a hundred time-staggered island journeys, while one honest agent pays only for its own.
